### Mockup 
![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/550c09cf-0747-452b-a24d-f4e074479f5a)
### Overview
We should have a "try demo" button on ubq.fi and this should bring the user to a "Start Demo UI" to be able to easily set up:
1. "Login with GitHub" to create a new demo repository in their GitHub. 
2. Install `ubiquity-os[bot]` - our production deployment.
3. Create the `.ubiquity-os` repository and push `.ubiquity-os.config.yml` with default settings (hardcoded evm wallet with no money should be fine.)
4. Add @ubiquity-os-simulant - a fake GitHub user profile with a personal access token that we can control with a GitHub Action PER plugin demo that runs on timers i.e. ~5 minutes with manual delays per action taken (i.e. leave a comment, open a pull request, file an issue) to simulate a team member that interacts with UbiquityOS. 
The "try demo" dashboard should have buttons for each of [these capabilities](https://github.com/ubiquity/business-development/issues/109#issuecomment-2579691293) that trigger the @ubiquity-os-simulant to run choreographed scenarios to demonstrate each capability. It should basically pretend to be the user's knowledgeable team member. 
Capabilities shortlist:
- Payouts
- `/ask`
- Task Matchmaking (I hope we don't pollute our vector embeddings data with these demos)
### Research Needed
- We need a webhook receiver inside the simulant that listens to requests from the "Start Demo UI"
   - It probably makes sense to just use a modified kernel, because it needs to invoke the "choreographed scenario plugins" 
- I realized that some events, like being assigned, requires a normal user profile and can't be done with a bot account, so we will need to make a fake user profile and control it with a personal access token. https://chatgpt.com/share/67ab5c0c-fc58-8001-87e1-cfab828d5819
### Deliverables
- [x] "Start Demo UI" - Forked from https://github.com/ubiquity/onboard.ubq.fi
- [x] @ubiquity-os-simulant user profile, and personal access token creation with correct permissions, and its webhook receiver code.
- [x] One choreographed scenario GitHub Action. For now, we can do a simple hello world that creates a new repository, opens a new issue, and calls the `/help` menu
### Next Steps
- We need to spec out the choreography of each scenario. 
- We also need to decide on one to get ready for the conference next week.

I think it would be safer to make people try this in a new repo. We talked a bit about it already, but we noticed that most of our potential partners were using closed-source. Having the bot installed and running on their repo would require already high elevations (admin permissions for org and such) which can be a blocker for closed-source organizations.
For the rest, instead of having a bot doing the actions, why not doing a tutorial and directly tell the user to do the actions? I am thinking like a `tutorial-ubiquity-os` bot that would tell you things like "Now, type in the command /start to start a task". It would be more interactive, would probably require less complex changes on our side and probably a better experience for the user.

Then if there is no interaction at all, why not simply make a video (with a proper montage, captions and everything) which requires no installation at all? I don't see the point of having to install everything if it is for a demo tbh, 30 seconds video would be more efficient.

But they can't play with it since we simulate everything, and as you said
So either we bypass that problem and they can fully interact with the bot despite not setting up this, and the demo bot seems more relevant, either they don't and they can't interact so the video makes more sense to me in such case.

@0x4007 Do you think a UI is needed for this? The user would still have to install the `GitHub App` through the GitHub UI no?
How about this:
We create a `demo-plugin`. This demo is triggerable via a command, say `/demo`.
No need to modify the kernel, it would run the command like any other command.
What the plugin does is that it uses a hard-coded configuration (this way the user trying out the demo wouldn't need to setup any configuration on its side) where we can set an empty wallet, and all the values we want.
That plugin follows the simple script you mentioned, doing actions in order within the given issue where the user invoked the `/demo` command.
Only thing that needs to be changed in the kernel is to react to `/demo` even if there is no `.ubiquity-os.configuration.yml` provided.
With what I suggest we could disable these plugins entirely or putting empty wallets and disabling comment evaluation etc as we see fit, and the user testing would not be able to override these.
I have to thoroughly evaluate all the aspects but it seems so far to be the simplest route to achieve a demo that is entirely scripted while using our real plugins
